answer: Jade Pulse Gate. Each identity must submit one small transaction per randomly chosen 45-second slot; the slot is revealed only after it passes, so an operator running many clones cannot schedule them from one script without distinct persistent processes. A dune of queued clones still collapses because idle slots are missed and identities are suspended. Every identity therefore costs a separate always-on executor plus a copper-level fee per slot, scaling linearly with clone count.
